 Diyar Nurgozhay vs Alik Lorenz Pick, 11/21/2026 Predictions UFC Qatar Odds
 by Tony Sink - 11/17/2026 
 Diyar Nurgozhay vs Alik Lorenz 
 UFC Qatar 
 ABHA Arena in Doha, Qatar 
 Saturday, November 21, 2026 
 Diyar Nurgozhay will battle Alik Lorenz at UFC Qatar on Saturday, November 21, 2026. The opening line has Nurgozhay at -250 while Lorenz is coming in at +208.
 Diyar Nurgozhay comes into this bout with a record of 12-2-0. The 29-year-old steps on the scale at 205 lbs and measures 6'2". The southpaw fighter has an arm span of 74". Alik Lorenz measures in at 6'2" and records a weight of 205 lbs. The orthodox fighter steps into the Octagon with a record of 8-2-0. The 29-year-old extends his reach 77". In the category of significant strikes, Diyar Nurgozhay is landing 5.19 per minute and Alik Lorenz is connecting on 9.71 significant strikes per minute. Nurgozhay lands 61% of the significant strikes he attempts and Lorenz lands 54%. In terms of defending in the Octagon, Nurgozhay absorbs 2.81 significant strikes per minute while Lorenz allows 10.40. Nurgozhay also deflects 59% of the significant strikes his opponents throw his way and Lorenz defends against 28% of the shots thrown.

 Concerning wrestling, Diyar Nurgozhay is the more skilled grappler as he takes his opponents to the mat 1.19 times per 15 minutes. Nurgozhay is finishing his takedown attempts on 75% of his tries and is stopping 72% of all takedowns attempted on him. Lorenz is taking his opponents down on 15% of his takedown tries and stuffing 15% of all takedowns attempted on him. In terms of going for the sub, Nurgozhay is the lesser skilled of the two fighters by trying 0.3 submissions per 15 min while Lorenz goes for 0.9 submissions per 15 min.

 In his previous fight, Diyar Nurgozhay faced Bruno Lopes and got a win for the night by way of a punch to the head in round 1. Lopes ended up landing 14 of 25 total strikes that he let go in that contest. Nurgozhay finished this fight landing 48 of 70 total strikes. Concerning significant strikes, Lopes landed 14 of 25, which means his percentage was 56%. He ended up landing 2 of 11 significant strikes aimed at the head. On the other side of the Octagon, Nurgozhay ended up landing 68% of his significant strikes by sticking 48 of 70. Out of all the significant strikes thrown, he landed 17 of 30 aimed at the head. 100% of the significant strikes landed by Lopes and 70% of them landed by Nurgozhay were tallied at distance.
 In the last Octagon appearance for Alik Lorenz, he went up against Mahamed Aly and ended up getting the victory by a punch to the head while on the ground in round 1. Aly landed 100% of the significant strikes he attempted at distance while Lorenz landed 85% of the significant strikes he tried at a distance. Lorenz ended up landing 56% of the significant strikes he attempted by connecting on 27 of 48. He connected on 22 of 42 significant strikes directed at the head. Aly landed 14 of 24 significant strikes in that contest. Of all the significant strikes, he ended up landing 6 of 14 to the head. Regarding total strikes that he let go in that contest, Aly ended up connecting on 14 of 24 while Lorenz was 27 of 48 total strikes.
 Other fights on the card to watch 
 An additional bout that shouldn't be missed is when Jiri Prochazka squares up against Navajo Stirling. Prochazka walks into the Octagon with a mark of 32-6-1. The 34-year-old weighs 205 lbs and stands 6'3". The orthodox fighter has a reach of 80". Stirling stands 6'4" and will fight at 205 lbs. The orthodox fighter walks into the cage holding a record of 11-0-0. The 29-year-old has a wingspan of 79". In the wrestling category, Jiri Prochazka gets a takedown 0.49 times per 15 min while Navajo Stirling takes his opponents to the mat 0.82 times per 3 rounds. When it comes to striking, Prochazka tags his opponents 5.61 strikes/minute and is connecting on 55% of the strikes that he attempts. On the other side of the cage you've got Navajo Stirling, who tags the opposition on 55% of the strikes that he throws and connects on 6.47 per minute.
 If you're going to be watching the fights, don't miss when Kevin Vallejos is set to square up in the Octagon against Aljamain Sterling. Sterling looks to add a win to his record of 26-5-0. The 37-year-old weighs 145 lbs and stands in at 5'7". The orthodox fighter has a reach of 71". Vallejos measures in at 5'7" and weighs 145 lbs. The switch fighter walks into the Octagon holding a record of 18-1-0. The 24-year-old has a reach of 68". In terms of grappling, Aljamain Sterling defends against 44% of the takedowns fighters have tried and is finishing his takedowns on 32% of his attempts. Vallejos is finishing his takedown tries on 28% of the tries he takes and thwarts 84% of takedowns his opponents have tried. Concerning striking, Sterling takes 2.15 strikes per min while he connects on 4.26 strikes per minute. Vallejos, on the contrary, is taking 4.41 strikes/min and is landing 6.12 per min.
 Who will win tonight's UFC match against the spread?
 Tony Sink's Pick: Take Diyar Nurgozhay (-250)
